data.bottom_line: The avalanche danger is MODERATE for WIND SLABS above 2500'. The danger is LOW elsewhere. New snow and strong winds have loaded starting zones and created fresh drifts at upper elevations. A person can trigger an avalanche on wind-loaded slopes or areas where new snow has fallen on weak facets. The size, stiffness, and sensitivity of instabilities will increase as you gain elevation. Look out for dense or stiff drifts, shooting cracks, or hollow-sounding snow. Slopes near ridgelines, bowls, or along the sides of gullies are the most likely places to find trouble. Seeking out lower-angle slopes or windward aspects will lessen your chances of triggering a slide. ------------------------------------ UPCOMING EVENTS: State of the Snowpack: Thursday, December 3rd - 6PM @ Backcountry Bike and Ski Free Avalanche Rescue Workshop: Saturday, December 12th – 12PM-3PM @ Hatcher Pass – Fishhook (Marmot) Lot
